title: Protecting Astronomical Interferometry through Quantum-Memory Scrambling
summary: Preserving the complex visibility of coherently captured starlight is essential for quantum-assisted long-baseline interferometry, because this nonlocal coherence carries the spatial information needed to form astronomical images. Yet finite memory lifetime and imperfect retrieval inevitably produce storage failures; when a failed cell is heralded, its erased subsystem can leak which-node information to the environment and dephase the stored coherence. Strict finite-dimensional (\(U(1)\)) covariance further forbids uniform exact correction of all single-memory erasures. We address this…
